page.layout: One printed page: running head at top; text in one column; Hebrew words set inline and in display lines; a verse-style list of forms in centred lines; no margin notes; catchword-style mark at foot is a signature-like sign and is not printed text.

main_text.l: Quæ autem in Kal sunt neutra, hic fiunt
הלך hillech, fecit ambulare, seu duxit.
Quæ vero in Kal non habentur, & hic
extant, sunt transitiva, ut, תקן tikken,
Verba, quæ in tertia persona singulari,
ab ה hi, vel ה he, sequente gutturali,

page.notes: Hebrew forms in the Hiphil paradigm are transcribed from the printed letters as far as legible; the vowel points and dots of the Hebrew display lines are not reproduced exactly and may need checking against the scan. The Latin-letter transliterations were read as printed, with hyphenated line-end breaks rejoined (hiph-kadt, hiphkad-tem). The printed "h" transliterations appear in italics in the source; they are shown here in plain text. The line "Hiphkid..." includes "Hiphkidu, hiphkad-tem" split across lines in the original.
